the prevalence of DM is high and increasing in Malaysia.
the prevalence of diabetes in children and adolescents in Malaysia was 0.3% and that 69% of the patients had T1DM.
the e-DiCAR has been successful in collecting information on the number and characteristics of diabetic patients in Malaysia.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: a) to describe the prevalence of type 1 diabetes in children and adolescents in Malaysia; b) to identify the socio-demographic and clinical characteristics associated with type 1 diabetes; c) to determine the prevalence of type-1 diabetes in children in the different regions in Malaysia.
the development of an on-line registry for the collection of information from patients with diabetes mellitus (T1DM, T2DM and MODY).
the prevalence of DM, the socio-demographic profile, the outcome of interventions and to facilitate research using the DiCARE database.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DiCARE is a useful tool for monitoring and evaluating diabetes care for children and adolescents in Malaysia.
DiCARE is the first of its kind in the world.
there is a need for more comprehensive data collection to determine the true prevalence of diabetes among the young in Malaysia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DiCARE is an effective tool for the surveillance of diabetes in children and adolescents.
the registry is useful to determine the number, the trend of DM patients, their socio- demographics and facilitate research using the registry.
the registry is a useful tool for the surveillance of DM patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many children with DM in Malaysia and they need more attention and care.
we are able to provide the first ever comprehensive national registry on DM among the children and adolescents in Malaysia.
we need to have a national register of diabetes in children and adolescents to facilitate research and improve the standard of diabetes care in the young.
